name: Nekta New York
evidenceSummary: Merchant FAQ explicitly accepts Bitcoin, Ether, Bitcoin Cash and USDC, with telephone assistance for payment. The same page identifies its single visitable showroom at 74 West 47th Street and says store visits are by appointment.
reason: Current merchant-owned payment FAQ and exact showroom address; payment rail unspecified.

name: Robotic Hair Restoration Center — New York
evidenceSummary: Official BTC for Hair Restoration page offers Bitcoin payment through BitPay for hair restoration at its Los Angeles and New York City offices. The page lists the New York office at 345 W. Broadway and telephone 212-763-7716.
reason: Dedicated merchant-owned Bitcoin payment instructions and physical office; appointments required. No payment rail inferred from processor.

name: PubKey NYC
evidenceSummary: Official FAQ states both PubKey bars take dollars and bitcoin and gives the NYC address as 85 Washington Pl. NYC's own home page describes burgers, hot dogs, wings and beer at that address.
reason: Explicit current merchant-owned acceptance and address; FAQ does not identify payment rail.

name: Doctor's Island Brewing Company
evidenceSummary: Square's October 8, 2025 firsthand owner case study says customers earn bitcoin rewards through Oshi and can spend bitcoin for beer. A separate Square beginner guide quotes owner Greg Hoffmeister accepting Bitcoin Payments for beer. Current brewery website confirms address and public taproom hours.
reason: Dated firsthand owner testimony on payment provider's own site, with current merchant-owned physical address. Square discloses compensating the business for participation; do not infer rails from Square/Oshi names alone.

name: Porcupine Real Estate
evidenceSummary: Official brokerage page displays Crypto Accepted Here and Bitcoin Accepted Here, describes its completed all-bitcoin real estate transaction and helping buyers purchase homes with Bitcoin, and lists its office at 157 Amory St, West Manchester, NH 03102.
reason: Current brokerage-owned acceptance page and exact office address. Arrange transaction terms first; a brokerage's acceptance does not mean every seller/property accepts Bitcoin.

name: Endodontic Specialists — Dr. Stanislav Moline
address: 1050 Sullivan Ave, Suite B2, South Windsor, CT 06074
evidenceSummary: Doctor.com provider profile says the practice accepts major credit cards, bitcoin and PayPal. Other provider directories corroborate the South Windsor office, but this pass could not retrieve an identifiable current merchant-owned payment policy.
reason: Directory payment assertion alone is insufficient to promote as merchant-confirmed. Official practice privacy form identifies Dr. Moline and the same phone but lists a mailing PO box, which must not be mapped.

name: The Jefferson / Jefferson & Co.
evidenceSummary: Rhode Island Bitcoin Meetup organizers describe The Jefferson accepting sats for food and drink and ask participants to bring a Lightning wallet. Merchant's current website confirms the visitable restaurant at 1946 Post Road, but no merchant-owned Bitcoin payment statement was located.
reason: Strong current community-organizer corroboration, not direct merchant confirmation. Check existing BTC Map record for same premises/name before considering a new pin; do not confuse with Jefferson Diner at 175 Jefferson Blvd.

name: iPie Pizzeria
evidenceSummary: Local chalet operator's restaurant guide explicitly says iPie takes Bitcoin and gives the restaurant address and phone. Its linked former merchant domain redirects to current iPie website, where this pass found no Bitcoin payment statement.
reason: Third-party local guide with undated payment claim, not a current merchant-owned policy. Do not treat the chalet guide's first-person quotation as the chalet accepting Bitcoin.

name: Folino's Pizza — Shelburne
evidenceSummary: Vermont Public's April 7, 2014 local reporting says Folino's Shelburne had been set up for Bitcoin payments by an employee. Merchant's current website lists five Vermont towns served but did not expose a current Bitcoin payment policy in this pass.
reason: Historical acceptance only. Do not automatically extend a 2014 Shelburne claim to newer branches or infer a current street address.

name: West Meadow Rabbits
evidenceSummary: Merchant-owned homepage explicitly says it accepts Bitcoin and describes its family rabbitry in Chester, New Hampshire, formerly Haverhill, Massachusetts.
reason: Payment acceptance is merchant-confirmed, but no public visitable street address was established. Do not pin private residence or old Haverhill location; arrange pickup before travel.

name: Murphy's Taproom — Manchester
evidenceSummary: December 22, 2022 contemporaneous account reproduces owner Keith Murphy's court testimony that his restaurant had accepted bitcoin since 2013. This is distinct from the Bitcoin ATM discussed in the same testimony.
reason: Dated firsthand owner testimony but current merchant payment policy and current address not retrieved. Do not mistake ATM availability for current food/drink acceptance.

name: Great Wave Sushi
evidenceSummary: January 26, 2025 self-identified food-truck owner announced their first BTC payment, naming Great Wave Sushi's Instagram account and a poke nachos sale. Current merchant site has a public event calendar; local venues corroborate continued mobile appearances in 2026.
reason: Potentially useful mobile merchant with dated self-identified owner evidence, but no permanent street location and social account identity not independently authenticated. Do not pin a past brewery stop or assume Lightning from commenters' suggestions.

name: Great Lost Bear
evidenceSummary: April 9, 2018 firsthand interview with owner Dave Evans and marketing manager Dave Foster describes customers paying for meals and beer with bitcoin and staff scanning a payment code. This is merchant payment evidence independent of the article's separate ATM/exchange subject.
reason: Historical owner/staff confirmation only; this pass found no current merchant-owned acceptance policy. Do not promote old evidence as a current confirmation.

name: HIFI Donuts — former 30 City Center location
evidenceSummary: March 25, 2025 local publication reproduces owners Melissa and Ari Modugno's announcement that the shop was closing April 17, 2025 after failing to negotiate a lease. August 6, 2026 reporting says the former space was replaced by Winnie's Vintage. The still-live merchant website's Bitcoin acceptance footer is stale.
reason: Closed physical location overrides live but stale official payment/footer/address content. Exclude this address; a future reopening elsewhere would need new evidence. Follow-up: https://wcyy.com/hifi-donuts-winnies-vintage-portland-maine/
